title: When you land
body:
International arrival is Tokyo (Haneda or Narita, whichever has the better transpacific fare) — no direct US flight reaches Fukuoka, so a Tokyo connection is unavoidable. A ~13-hour flight lands mid-afternoon to evening; plan to overnight near the Tokyo airport rather than rushing a same-day domestic connection.

Buy an IC card (Suica/Pasmo) at the airport the moment you land — the 2023 chip-shortage sales suspension fully resolved by March 2025. Get an eSIM active before leaving the arrivals hall. The next morning, fly Tokyo → Fukuoka to start the trip.

title: Local essentials
body:
Cash matters more than in most countries you've traveled. Yatai stalls run roughly 90% cash-only, and plenty of small ramen counters and markets are cash-only too. 7-Eleven ATMs (Seven Bank) are the reliable fallback — Visa, Mastercard, Amex, JCB, Discover and UnionPay, 24/7, ~28,000 machines nationwide, for a per-withdrawal fee on top of your home bank's. Carry {{fact:local-essentials-1000}} notes — stalls often can't break a {{fact:local-essentials-10000}} bill.

Tipping doesn't happen anywhere in Japan — restaurants, taxis, hotels, guides.

Power: 100V, Type A plugs (US shape, lower voltage) — most modern chargers auto-handle 100–240V, but check the brick before assuming.

title: Entry & documents
moreLabel: Tax-free shopping — the Nov 1 system change
body:
US passport holders enter visa-free for tourism, up to 90 days. Visit Japan Web (pre-filed immigration/customs QR) is optional, not required — paper landing cards still work planeside.

Tax-free shopping straddles a system change mid-trip. Purchases through Oct 31, 2026 use the current instant-discount system: passport at checkout, tax-free price applied on the spot, {{fact:tax-free-threshold-5000}} (pre-tax) minimum per store per day, items stay sealed until departure. From {{fact:tax-free-cutover-nov-1}}, Japan switches to refund-at-departure: pay the full tax-inclusive price at checkout, then scan your passport at an airport departure kiosk before check-in. Practical read for the shopping days: do bigger purchases in Fukuoka and Hokkaido by Oct 31; anything bought in Sendai in November needs full sticker price at checkout and extra kiosk time at the Tokyo departure airport.

title: Phone & data
body: For ~26 days of data, an eSIM is cheapest and most flexible — and matters more here than usual, since the group splits (2 fly home Nov 2) and a shared pocket-wifi puck stops working the moment you're not together. Ubigi's 10GB/30-day plan runs {{fact:ubigi-10gb-30day-1650}}, unlimited/30-day {{fact:ubigi-unlimited-30day-65}} — activation is clean, the plan starts the moment you validate it in-app. ⚠ "Unlimited" plans on every major eSIM provider (Ubigi, Airalo, Holafly) have a repeated, unresolved complaint about throttling past a daily threshold — budget for the higher tier if you're shooting a lot of photo/video. Buy before you land (installs over home wifi, activates on arrival).

title: Booking checklist
body: Domestic flights (Tokyo→Fukuoka, Fukuoka→Sapporo) anchor the shared part of the trip; the Sapporo→Sendai leg and the return-home flight are only for the 2 continuing past Nov 2 — see the traveler questions in the intake doc for the still-open accommodation and routing decisions. The Zao Onsen ryokan is worth locking in as soon as dates are firm — it's a small, historic property, not a chain with endless rooms.
checklist: Transpacific flights — into Tokyo (HND/NRT), and home for the 2 leaving Nov 2
Domestic flights: Tokyo → Fukuoka, Fukuoka → Sapporo, then Sapporo → Sendai (2 continuing only)
Confirm each traveler's departure airport (unconfirmed — no globe route drawn yet)
Confirm the Oct 29–Nov 2 vs. Nov 3–5 accommodation split for the 2 continuing (open question)
Miyamaso Takamiya ryokan, Zao Onsen — book directly (reserve.489ban.net) once dates are firm
Accommodation — Fukuoka (Tenjin/Hakata), Sapporo (Susukino/Odori), Sendai (near the station) — all under $100/night except the ryokan night
eSIM (Ubigi/Airalo) for each traveler — buy before departure, install over home wifi
JR Kyushu rail pass (Northern, 5-day) and/or JR East–South Hokkaido Rail Pass, if the point-to-point fare comparison favors them
Pokémon GO Wild Area Sendai tickets — sales not yet open as of this check; watch pokemongo.com and buy immediately once they open, past events have sold out
US State Dept travel advisory — bot-gated against automated fetches this pass; needs a live browser check before travel
Any timed museum/attraction tickets that come up once dates are locked
